Q: Can i display blog titles from my blog on another external website using iframe, HTML and CSS A:

Using only iframe, HTML, and CSS, it is not possible to dynamically fetch and display blog post titles from another website.

HTML and CSS are static technologies. They cannot:

  • Fetch external data

  • Parse another site’s content

  • Extract specific elements such as post titles

  • Communicate with another domain

An <iframe> can only embed an entire webpage. It does not allow selective access to or extraction of content from that page.

Due to the browser’s same-origin policy, the contents of an iframe loaded from another domain cannot be accessed or styled.

For dynamic retrieval of blog titles, at least one of the following is required:

  • Server-side code (PHP, Python, etc.)

  • Client-side JavaScript

  • RSS or REST API consumption

  • WordPress plugins or feeds

  • Third-party embed services

Without using any of these, dynamic content retrieval is not possible.

Q: I am trying create tags with a custom template type outside of GTM's TAG UI but through GTM container import A:

Custom templates:

Type is set to cvt_containerId_templateId

Gallery Templates

Type is cvt_galleryTemplateId

So based if the asset (tag or variable) you are trying to import is from the Gallery (you will know as the template object will have the galleryReference key) then you shoul use cvt_galleryTemplateId .

Submit this script to your LLM to let it understand the logic:

for template in templates:
if 'galleryReference' in template:
# Gallery template - import from Community Gallery
gallery_ref = template['galleryReference']
try:
imported = gtm.accounts().containers().workspaces().templates().import_from_gallery(
parent=dest_workspace_path,
acknowledgePermissions=True,
galleryOwner=gallery_ref['owner'],
galleryRepository=gallery_ref['repository'],
gallerySha=gallery_ref['version']
).execute()

                    gallery_template_id = imported.get('galleryReference', {}).get('galleryTemplateId')  
                    log(f"  ✓ Imported gallery template: {template.get('name')} (cvt\_{gallery_template_id})")  
                    templates_imported += 1  
                except Exception as e:  
                    result\['warnings'\].append(f"Failed to import template {template.get('name')}: {str(e)}")  
                    log(f"  ✗ Failed to import: {template.get('name')} - {str(e)}")  
            else:  
                \# Custom template - copy templateData and create new template  
                if 'templateData' in template:  
                    try:  
                        \# Create custom template with templateData  
                        custom_template_body = {  
                            "name": template\['name'\],  
                            "templateData": template\['templateData'\]  
                        }  

                        created_template = gtm.accounts().containers().workspaces().templates().create(  
                            parent=dest_workspace_path,  
                            body=custom_template_body  
                        ).execute()  

                        \# Build the cvt type mapping: old cvt_X_Y -\> new cvt_A_B  
                        old_container_id = template.get('containerId')  
                        old_template_id = template.get('templateId')  
                        old_type = f"cvt\_{old_container_id}\_{old_template_id}"  

                        new_container_id = created_template.get('containerId')  
                        new_template_id = created_template.get('templateId')  
                        new_type = f"cvt\_{new_container_id}\_{new_template_id}"  

                        template_type_mapping\[old_type\] = new_type  

                        log(f"  ✓ Copied custom template: {template.get('name')} ({old_type} → {new_type})")  
                        templates_imported += 1  
                    except Exception as e:  
                        result\['warnings'\].append(f"Failed to copy custom template {template.get('name')}: {str(e)}")  
                        log(f"  ✗ Failed to copy custom template: {template.get('name')} - {str(e)}")  
                else:  
                    result\['warnings'\].append(f"Template {template.get('name')} has no templateData - skipped")  
                    log(f"  ⚠ Skipped template: {template.get('name')} (no templateData)")

Q: Python package installed in environment recognized A:

If a Python package installed in your Anaconda environment is not recognized , you can follow these troubleshooting steps:

  1. Active the Correct Environment: Ensure that you have activated the Anaconda environment where the package is installed. Use this following command -

                 conda activate your_env_name

  2. Check Installed Packages: Verify that the package is installed in the active environment by running:

                    conda list

    or

                    pip list

Install the Package: If the package is not listed, you may need to install it. You can do this using either conda Or pip:

  • Using conda:

                    conda install package_name

  • Using pip:

                     pip install package_name4.

    4.Check Python Path: Make sure your Python interpreter is pointing to the correct Anaconda environment. You can check this with:

    import sys

    print(sys.executable)
